brief.headline: KOR memory names sold off Mon 29-Jun on $518B fab pledge; HBM4 ramp intact, DRAM/NAND Q2 pricing +58-75% QoQ, CoWoS tight thru '27
brief.summary: <cite index="42-11,42-14">Samsung and SK Hynix declined Monday after unveiling a combined 800 trillion won ($518B) southwest fab investment</cite>, signaling <cite index="41-18">shares fell 4.86% and 1.68% respectively despite the capex commitment</cite>. <cite index="17-1,17-15">TrendForce projects Q2 2026 DRAM contract prices up 58-63% QoQ and NAND up 70-75% QoQ</cite>, with <cite index="4-20">Micron guiding 68% gross margin in Q2 2026 and top-three memory makers' HBM output fully allocated for the year</cite>. <cite index="30-4,30-6">TSMC's CoWoS supply-demand gap is narrowing from 20% to ~10% by end-2026 as monthly capacity reaches 120-140K wafers</cite>, but <cite index="31-1,31-30">CoWoS remains fully booked with Nvidia holding ~60% of 2026 allocation</cite>.
brief.pair_trade_view: <cite index="38-28,38-29">SK Hynix holds 58% HBM market share as of June 2026 with capacity sold out through 2026 into 2027</cite>, while <cite index="42-7">Samsung is investing heavily to narrow the technology gap with its domestic rival</cite>. <cite index="38-6">Samsung has reportedly begun shipping HBM4 and initiated a 'Super-Gap Roadmap' to reclaim market leadership</cite>. <cite index="9-7,9-8">SK Hynix expects minimal to modest HBM3E pricing downtick for 2026 vs 2025, with HBM4 commanding ~40% premium over prior generation even after absorbing 50% cost-per-bit increase</cite>. <cite index="38-24,38-25">SK Hynix Q1 2026 revenue hit 52.6 trillion won (+198% YoY) with 72% operating margin</cite>. Near-term, SK Hynix sustains structural HBM share advantage; Samsung faces qualification timing risk but longer-duration upside if HBM4 ramp accelerates. Both vulnerable to capex fatigue concerns post-announcement selloff.

memory_cycle.notes: <cite index="16-1,16-8">DRAM and NAND in structural reallocation to HBM, not cyclical shortage, with prices elevated through 2027 and long-term floor reset above historical levels</cite>. <cite index="14-2,14-3">Q1 2026 conventional DRAM contract prices rose 90-95% QoQ, the largest quarterly increase on record</cite>. <cite index="16-13">HBM3E consumes 3x wafer area of standard DDR5, every HBM wafer reduces DDR5 supply by 3 wafers of capacity</cite>. <cite index="4-18">Bank of America forecasts global DRAM revenue +51% in 2026 and NAND +45%, with ASPs climbing >30%</cite>. <cite index="16-12">New fab capacity will not arrive in volume before late 2027, with meaningful relief into 2028 or 2029</cite>. Pricing power intact but <cite index="1-9,1-10">TurboQuant AI optimization technique release caused sharp memory provider selloff, though structural demand shift remains uncertain</cite>.

brief.hbm_pulse: <cite index="5-4">SK Hynix reported 5x jump in quarterly profit in April, says HBM demand exceeds supply over next three years</cite>. <cite index="9-6">HBM bit shipments projected to jump 35% in 2026 to 17.1 billion gigabits</cite>. <cite index="4-16,4-27">SK Hynix is only supplier able to deliver both HBM3E and HBM4 at scale; UBS forecasts ~70% HBM4 market share for Nvidia's Rubin platform in 2026</cite>. <cite index="2-1,2-6">Micron in high-volume production of HBM4 36GB 12H achieving >11 Gb/s pin speeds with >2.8 TB/s bandwidth, 2.3x bandwidth and >20% power efficiency improvement over HBM3E</cite>. <cite index="6-14">Global memory shortage enabling Micron, SK Hynix, Samsung to hike prices</cite>. <cite index="4-12">HBM3E consumes roughly 3x the wafer area of standard DDR5 due to larger dies and yield losses from vertical stacking</cite>. Supply remains binding constraint despite hyperscaler capex surge.

news_pulse.headline: Samsung, SK Hynix unveil $518B Korea southwest fab investment; shares fall 4.9%, 1.7% on Mon 29-Jun
news_pulse.implication: Record-scale capex commitment (800 trillion won for 4 new fabs) signals structural demand confidence but market sold off on overcapacity/ROI concerns and lack of timeline detail. S&P says both have financial flexibility to absorb near-term Yongin acceleration.

news_pulse.headline: TrendForce: Q2 2026 DRAM contract prices +58-63% QoQ, NAND +70-75% QoQ; Q1 was +90-95%
news_pulse.implication: Unprecedented pricing power continues but DRAM rate decelerating from Q1 record. NAND now accelerating faster than DRAM for first time this cycle as enterprise SSD demand absorbs capacity. CSPs securing supply via long-term agreements.

news_pulse.headline: Hyperscaler 2026 AI capex now ~$700B, up from $400B in 2025; Meta raised guide to $125-145B
news_pulse.implication: Alphabet $35.7B Q1 capex (>2x YoY), Microsoft $30.9B (+84% YoY), Amazon tracking $200B FY26. Meta guidance raise cited higher component pricing. Amazon FCF down 95% TTM to $1.2B. Memory demand structural but ROI scrutiny intensifying.

news_pulse.headline: TSMC CoWoS supply-demand gap narrowing to ~10% by end-2026 from 20% now; capacity 120-140K wafers/mo
news_pulse.implication: CoWoS fully booked through 2026, Nvidia ~60% of allocation. Monthly capacity scaling from 75-80K currently to 120-140K by Dec-26. OSAT partners (ASE, Amkor, UMC) adding 50-60K wafers/mo. CoPoS pilot production mid-2027, Nvidia Feynman first customer.

news_pulse.headline: SK Hynix 58% HBM market share Q4 2025; Samsung 22%, Micron 21%; HBM4 ramp underway
news_pulse.implication: SK Hynix Q1 revenue 52.6T won (+198% YoY), 72% op margin. UBS projects SK Hynix maintains ~50% HBM bit share in 2026, commands ~40% HBM4 premium over HBM3E. Micron HBM4 in high-volume production. Memory shortage expected through 2027.

news_pulse.headline: Micron, SK Hynix cross $1T market cap; SK Hynix +1,000% over 12mo; Samsung hit $1T earlier in May
news_pulse.implication: SK Hynix rose 9.3% Wed 27-May, Micron surged 19% Tue 26-May (strongest since 2011) after UBS double PT. HBM identified as tightest AI infrastructure chokepoint. Investor bet: supply shortage duration outlasts historical cyclicality.

news_pulse.headline: Memory ASPs +30%+ in 2026; lead times >40 weeks; Dell COO: 'never seen costs move at this rate'
news_pulse.implication: Memory now 35% of PC build materials vs 20% a year ago. Dell, Lenovo, HP, HPE raised server prices 15% late-2025/early-2026; Dell added 17% increase 30-Mar-26. Counterpoint: DDR5 64GB RDIMM could double by end-2026 vs early-2025.

news_pulse.headline: TurboQuant AI technique release caused sharp memory stock selloff; Deutsche Bank flags continuous AI disruption
news_pulse.implication: Samsung +114% YTD, SK Hynix +186% YTD as of 25-May. TurboQuant announcement triggered sell-off across memory providers. Deutsche Bank: remains to be seen if structural demand shift. Bull case: AI shakes off cyclicality. Bear case: history of boom/bust.

brief.derivatives_signal: No KRX derivatives flow cited in payload. Monitor SK Hynix July 10 Nasdaq ADR listing ($29.4B raise at $166/share, HSBC sees 20% upside) for US option open-interest build and ADR/local arb. KOSPI closed +2.3% Wed 27-May after 5.1% intraday spike forced program-buying halt. Recent sharp single-day drops (up to 12.5% late June per Google Finance) signal elevated vol regime. Memory names trading on AI demand sustainability vs capex fatigue; recommend watching HBM4 qualification timelines and hyperscaler Q2 capex execution as vol catalysts.
